page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 2835 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across memory bandwidth and specialized compute tasks. The server achieved a strong read-only cached memory bandwidth of 3631.83 GB/sec and a large-block uncached write bandwidth of 100.8 GB/sec. In Geekbench testing, the system demonstrated strong single-core and multi-core capabilities, with top-tier performance in image processing at 20232.0. The processor's support for Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions contributes to strong Passmark extended instructions scores and efficient LLM inference, reaching 342.39 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48ds_v6 offers a balanced resource density, combining high-frequency dedicated Intel Xeon cores with substantial local storage capacity. This profile makes it highly suitable for database operations, as evidenced by a strong Passmark database score of 25573.3 and Redis SET performance of 67.91 million operations per second. The server is well-suited for workloads such as relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
